items.title: An algebra over a field is etale exactly when it is a finite product of finite separable extensions
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file algebra.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma characterises etale algebras over a field as finite products of finite separable extensions (statement lines 39610-39615). The proof does not compute differentials: it reduces to the factors of a finite product by stability of etaleness, treats a field extension directly, and in the converse direction deduces separability from smoothness at the generic point (proof lines 39617-39649). Deciding to split into factors first, so that only a field extension has to be analysed, is the step that shortens the argument. H2.
